claims.text: MoSi2 is initially in a conventional polycrystalline ceramic form.
A graded, nanostructured MoSi2 interlayer is introduced between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed interlayer is intended for exposure to high thermal gradients.
The proposed interlayer is intended for exposure to intense neutron irradiation.
A graded MoSi2 nanostructure can accommodate thermal-stress transitions between W and CuCrZr.
A graded MoSi2 nanostructure can accommodate mechanical-stress transitions between W and CuCrZr.
The MoSi2 interlayer reduces residual stress by providing a gradual transition between the thermal expansion coefficients of W and CuCrZr.
The MoSi2 interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier against interfacial mixing under irradiation.
The nanostructured MoSi2 interlayer improves thermal-mechanical stability relative to a direct W-CuCrZr bond.
The nanostructured MoSi2 interlayer improves interfacial adhesion relative to a direct W-CuCrZr bond.
The nanostructured MoSi2 interlayer reduces bonded-interface degradation relative to a direct W-CuCrZr bond.
The beneficial effect is expected to persist up to operating temperatures typical of fusion reactors.
The beneficial effect is expected to persist up to radiation fluxes typical of fusion reactors.
Performance outside the stated fusion-reactor operating conditions is unverified.
The choice of MoSi2 as the interlayer remains speculative because no direct eligible evidence is provided.
The optimal MoSi2 nanostructuring parameters remain speculative.
